summary: It plays like a leaner, more elegant remix of the original Great Western Trail, replacing the Kansas City hiring puzzle with a farmer-recruitment and grain-economy system that feels tighter and less fiddly. Games tend to be faster and slightly less brain-burning than the original while keeping the same core tension of engine-building on your player board versus racing the rondel to Buenos Aires.
praised: Cleaner, more streamlined rules than the original GWT
Farmer/grain mechanic adds a fresh, well-integrated twist
Strong player board upgrade puzzle and engine building
Shorter playtime and less downtime than the original
criticised: Less iconic/thematic than the cowboy original for some fans
Some feel it's a bit too similar to GWT rather than a bold new game
Map/route choices can feel less dramatic than the original's shortcuts
Still a heavy-ish rules overhead for newcomers

interaction.kind: route/tile drafting and light blocking on the shared board

scoring.why: Points come from cattle deliveries, buildings, city/boat tiles, objectives, and engine efficiency, so the winner is decided by who builds the best combination of scoring sources.
